evidence.section_title: A Comparison of the Relative Efficacy of  Self-Control Therapy and a Behavioral  Problem-Solving Therapy for Depression  in Children
evidence.quote: [/page/0/Text/3] Twenty-nine children 9 to 12 years old who were identified as moderately to severely depressed using the Children's Depression Inventory were randomly assigned to either a self-control, behavioral problem-solving, or waiting list condition.

[page/2/Text/8] A total of 372 children in the fourth, fifth, and sixth grades of a semirural elementary school were screened with the Children's Depression Inventory (CDI; Kovacs, 1981) for inclusion in the study. [page/3/Text/5] Parental permission for additional assessment was obtained for 39 (64%) of the children who initially scored in excess of 16 on the CDI. ... Thirty-one of the children received a total score of 13 or more on the second administration. One subject was later excluded from the study and referred to an external agency when the clinical interview (Childen's Depression Rating Scale-Revised; Poznanski et al., 1984) revealed additional serious nondepressive pathology.
[/page/5/Text/9] This screening procedure identified 61 children (16.4~ who scored in excess of 16 on the CDI.

[/page/5/Text/12] The 31 students with scores equal to or exceeding 13 on this second administration of the CDI were individually interviewed within a week with [/page/6/Text/2] the CDRS-R by the first author, who was blind to subjects' exact CDI scores.

[/page/7/Text/3] Subjects were randomly assigned to experimental conditions. [/page/7/Text/4] Common Elements. Subjects in the self-control and behavioral problem-solving conditions received a behavioral rationale for the development and treatment of depression. [/page/9/Text/4] Waiting List. Following random assignment to conditions, subjects in the waiting list (WL) condition were informed that they would begin meeting with a therapist as soon as possible.

[/page/13/Text/3] At pretesting, all of the subjects had scores in excess of 13 on the CDI. At posttesting, 7 of 9 subjects (78%) in the S-C condition, 6 of 10 subjects (60~ in the BPS condition, and 1 of 9 subjects (11%) in the WL condition had scores below 13. Fewer subjects exhibited clinically significant levels of depression on the CDRS-R prior to treatment. Fifty-six percent of the subjects in the S-C condition, 20% of the subjects in the BPS condition, and none of the subjects in the WL condition had scores in excess of 40 on the CDRS-R prior to treatment.

evidence.section_title: A Comparison of the Relative Efficacy of  Self-Control Therapy and a Behavioral  Problem-Solving Therapy for Depression  in Children
evidence.quote: [/page/0/Text/3] Twenty-nine children 9 to 12 years old who were identified as moderately to severely depressed using the Children's Depression Inventory were randomly assigned to either a self-control, behavioral problem-solving, or waiting list condition.
[page/2/Text/8] A total of 372 children ... were screened with the Children's Depression Inventory (CDI; Kovacs, 1981) for inclusion in the study.

['/page/4/Text/6', 'The Children\'s Depression Inventory (Kovacs, 1981) is the most commonly used self-report measure of  depression for children 7 to 17 years of age.'] ['/page/4/Text/7', 'The Child Depression Scale (CDS; Reynolds, in press), a self-report  measure for children 8 to 13, was also employed to assess the severity of  depression.'] ['/page/4/Text/8', 'The Children\'s Depression Rating Scale-Revised (CDRS-R; Poznanski et al., 1984) is a semistructured interview  schedule appropriate for children ages 6 to 12. The CDRS-R consists of 17  depression-related items'] ['/page/4/Text/9', 'The internalizing, depression, and social withdrawal subscales were employed.']

The Coopersmith Self-Esteem Inventory measures an individual's personal evaluation of his or her own worth [/page/5/Text/3]; The Revised Children's Manifest Anxiety Scale (RCMAS, Reynolds & Richmond, 1978), a commonly used self-report measure of manifest anxiety in children, was used. [/page/5/Text/4]
[/page/5/Text/9] The 372 students completed the CDI in their homerooms.

[/page/5/Text/11] At pretesting, the 39 students whose parents gave their permission completed the CDI, CDS, RCMAS, and CSEI. Their mothers were asked to complete and return the CBCL within a week. [/page/5/Text/12] The 31 students with scores equal to or exceeding 13 on this second administration of the CDI were individually interviewed within a week with [/page/6/Text/2] the CDRS-R by the first author, who was blind to subjects' exact CDI scores.
CDRS-R: [013_posttesting] interviews with the CDRS-R; CBCL: [013_posttesting] mothers were once again asked to complete the CBCL
[/page/6/Text/10] 23 of the 28 subjects completed the four self-report measures and the CDRS-R. Mothers were again contacted and asked to complete the CBCL within 3 days.

[/page/7/Text/4] Self-monitoring log sheets of pleasant activities were completed by subjects on a daily basis. [/page/8/Text/4] During the first four sessions, subjects were taught to monitor pleasant activities and positive self-statements through the use of log sheets, which consisted of lists of pleasant events and self-statements. On the bottom of each sheet, subjects rated their mood for the day on a 0-10 scale.
[/page/10/Text/5] Subjects in both treatments endorsed a significantly reduced level of depressive symptomatology on the CDI and CDS.

[/page/16/Table/2] CSEI; [/page/16/Table/2] CBCL-social withdrawal; [/page/16/Table/2] CBCL-depression
